title: Nomenclature — every name the records use for the same thing
method: Harvested from the Legal Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com; 794 pages read through the public REST API, 21 Oct 2026), its evidence register, transcripts and nomenclature pages. Each variant is the wording of the record cited; where no record was found it is marked SOURCE PENDING. “Wiki label” means a term the Wiki uses for analysis, not a word from a period record.

status_key.record: Wording seen in a held document or its transcription
status_key.record (OCR; page image not seen): Newspaper search-result text; page image not seen
status_key.catalogue: Archive catalogue wording; document not seen
status_key.secondary: A later source citing the record
status_key.identity unresolved: Source wording exists; whether it means the same thing is not proved

farmer_woman.question: Does a newspaper record Mary as “farmer woman”?
farmer_woman.answer: Not in those words. The Western Mail of 20 November 1958, p.7, headlined its report “It’s a Crichel Down, says woman farmer” about Mrs M. D. Buckler (EV-0037). The text is from newspaper search-result OCR; the page image has not been seen. No record found says “farmer woman”.
